18843: A use-after-free vulnerability was discovered in Adobe Flash Player when used with Internet Explorer. The vulnerability occurred during memory management and allowed arbitrary code execution due to improper validation of freed memory addresses. Exploitation of the vulnerability could have enabled attackers to execute malicious code.
163820: A vulnerability was found where sensitive account actions were performed via GET requests containing security tokens, which can be cached, remain in browser history, and get bookmarked, enabling potential CSRF attacks.
172289: A vulnerability was found in the HackerOne integrations design that could allow an attacker to connect a victim's HackerOne account to the attacker's Slack account without the victim's consent. This could be exploited through various techniques including clickjacking, social engineering, or by exploiting an XSS vulnerability. The attacker only needs to steal a click from the victim to exploit this. Steps to reproduce were provided. Supporting references demonstrate the issue.
397792: A vulnerability was discovered in which some email addresses defined in RFC2142 could be registered on hackerone.com, allowing takeover of addresses intended for specific network roles. The attacker demonstrated control of the trouble@wearehackerone.com address. To resolve the issue, hackerone.com implemented an exclusion list to prevent registering RFC2142-defined addresses.
401793: The vulnerability was an insecure deeplink feature that allowed sensitive information disclosure. The deeplink lacked proper validation, enabling attackers to load any URL within a webview that contained sensitive information. A temporary patch was distributed, and a permanent fix was subsequently released and fully rolled out.
401940: The Venmo Android application used a built-in URL parser that had a known logic problem with certain characters. This allowed an external URL to be passed to the application activity without proper validation, potentially exposing some session data to a third party.
410099: The account details page on the █████████ website was vulnerable to a CSRF attack. An attacker could have modified a victim's email address by tricking the victim into visiting a malicious web page. Once the victim's email was changed, the attacker could have requested a password reset and taken over the victim's account.
419891: A CSRF vulnerability in the /signup/email API endpoint at khanacademy.org allowed takeovers of accounts with unconfirmed email addresses. The endpoint insufficiently verified requests came from the authenticated user. An attacker could exploit this to associate accounts with their email address and then reset the password. The attack required the target user to visit an attacker website while logged in and have an unconfirmed email address.
424443: A vulnerability was found in the PayPal Android application's deeplink feature, which failed to validate the requested endpoint. This allowed a specifically crafted request from a website or separate app on the device to direct traffic to any destination. While the impact was limited by compensating controls, sensitive data could be collected by a malicious actor.
485748: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in the reporting functionality, allowing malicious scripts to be injected. This could lead to the theft of data when reports are viewed.
498845: On December 20th, 2016, a data migration was executed to provision a new payout preference for HackerOne employees. Due to an incorrect assumption, the payout preference was provisioned for 12 non-HackerOne employees. The issue was identified on February 19, 2019 and resolved the following day. No users received any bounties, and only the corporate email addresses of HackerOne employees were disclosed.
669776: The vulnerability allowed program contributors to receive emails disclosing the title of a report, even after the issue was considered resolved. This could potentially expose sensitive information to unauthorized individuals.
698708: The report discloses that removed staff members who had "Apps" permission could still modify Flow app connection settings due to improper authorization. Signed URLs generated by Shopify Flow used a timestamp that remained valid for only one hour. However, a removed staff member could keep refreshing the timestamp and path_hmac parameters to gain unauthorized access to Flow app connections indefinitely.
709378: The session was not properly expired upon logout. An attacker could have obtained the user's session cookies and accessed the user account, allowing changes to be made to the profile or deletion of the account.
732987: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered in a parameter of a URL for a web application. The vulnerability occurred because user-supplied input was not properly sanitized before being reflected in the application's responses. This allowed malicious JavaScript code to be executed in a victim's browser when they visited a specially crafted URL. The issue was demonstrated through a proof-of-concept and could have resulted in the attacker executing arbitrary script code in the browsers of authenticated users. Remediation was recommended through sanitizing user input and validating data at the server side to prevent injection of unauthorized script code.
733051: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered in the URL parameter of the "Choose a data source" page at "https://bi.owox.com/ui/settings/connected-services/setup/". When a malicious URL containing script code was entered, it was reflected back without sanitization, allowing the script to execute in a victim's browser and potentially carry out actions like hijacking sessions.
733222: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered in Smule.com that allowed malicious JavaScript code to be permanently stored on the website through vulnerable form fields. When victims viewed affected pages, the malicious script could be executed in their browsers, potentially allowing attackers to steal cookies or hijack user sessions.
737039: A vulnerability was found where old sessions did not expire after a password change. The issue has since been resolved.
737169: A vulnerability was found that allowed bypassing email verification and creating email templates with the editor. The issue has been resolved.
738899: A vulnerability was found where it was possible to change a password by entering an incorrect old password. The issue has since been resolved.
